blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why a spring stretches more when you hang a heavier object on it? This is explained by Hooke's Law.

blocks.markdown: Hooke's Law is a fundamental principle in physics that describes the behavior of springs and elastic materials. It states that the extension of a spring is directly proportional to the load applied to it, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded.

blocks.title: Hooke's Law
blocks.text: Hooke's Law states that the force $F$ applied to a spring is directly proportional to the extension $e$ of the spring, expressed as $F = ke$, where $k$ is the force constant.

blocks.markdown: The force constant, $k$, is a measure of the stiffness of the spring. A larger $k$ means a stiffer spring. The elastic limit is the maximum extent to which a material can be stretched without permanently deforming.

blocks.title: Calculating the Force Constant
blocks.prompt: A spring extends by 0.2 m when a force of 10 N is applied. Calculate the force constant of the spring.
blocks.answer: The force constant of the spring is 50 N/m.

blocks.markdown: To visualize Hooke's Law, you can sketch a load-extension graph. The graph is a straight line passing through the origin, up to the elastic limit. Beyond this point, the material may not return to its original shape.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When sketching a load-extension graph, remember to label the axes correctly and mark the elastic limit clearly.

points: Hooke's Law is expressed as $F = ke$, where $F$ is the force, $e$ is the extension, and $k$ is the force constant.
The elastic limit is the maximum extension before permanent deformation occurs.
